actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

inputs.description: Seed used by the next reset
inputs.name: seed

facts.text: The clone is a UR5e arm and Robotiq Hand-e gripper simulator with a state-based peg-in-hole Gymnasium environment and custom Gymnasium wrappers
ur5ePegInHoleGymEnv_easy-v0 is registered with entry point mujoco_sim.envs:ur5ePegInHoleGymEnv
The easy variant applies XYZGripperCloseEnv, SpacemouseIntervention, CustomObsWrapper and FlattenObservation
The easy variant ends with gymnasium's FlattenObservation wrapper
The base action space is a seven-element Box from -1.0 to 1.0
XYZGripperCloseEnv narrows the action space to the first three elements (x, y, z) of the base Box
The observation space is a Dict of nine Box members, each bounded by +-1e6
The easy variant keeps connector_pose, controller_pose, ur5e/tcp_pose, ur5e/tcp_vel, ur5e/wrist_force and ur5e/wrist_torque
CustomObsWrapper rebuilds the state Dict with only the kept keys
controller_pose is a six-element array: the controller position and its orientation
control_dt is 0.02 s and physics_dt is 0.002 s
n_substeps is int(control_dt // physics_dt), so one control step runs ten physics steps
_max_episode_steps is 1000.0
step sets truncated once _elapsed_steps reaches _max_episode_steps
step returns observation, reward, terminated, truncated and info
reset returns the observation and an empty info dict
reset accepts an optional seed argument
Port randomization draws with np.random.uniform from numpy's global generator, so the reset seed argument does not seed it
reward_shaping is False and sparse_reward_weights is 0 by default
The step returns the sparse reward while reward_shaping is False
task_complete_tolerance is 0.0025
The task is complete when the connector-to-port distance is below the tolerance
The default Cartesian workspace bounds are [0.2, -0.3, 0.0] to [0.6, 0.3, 0.05]
The environment declares the render modes human and rgb_array
The clone pins mujoco 3.2.5 and gymnasium 1.0.0

determinism.notes: the fake seeds Python's random.Random from reset(seed) and is deterministic afterwards, so one seed repeats a trajectory of this package; the upstream reset accepts a seed but draws the port and controller randomization from numpy's global generator (ur5e_pick_gym_connector.py:276-279), so a seed does not fix those draws upstream and the two backends do not start from the same state

gaps: the deployed model is MuJoCo rigid-body dynamics with contacts (F1), but the fake backend is a pure-Python kinematic stand-in: it models no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, actuator forces, sensors or noise, and its start positions and step scale are placeholders
the fake does not model the peg-in-hole task, the reward or task-success termination: it returns the sparse -1 reward, never terminates for success and only truncates at 1000 steps
the fake uses Python's random.Random for its start noise while the upstream reset accepts a seed but draws from numpy's global generator, so one seed gives different starting states on the two

the easy variant's SpacemouseIntervention wrapper opens a SpaceMouse or a keyboard at construction and ur5ePegInHoleGymEnv.__init__ calls glfw and creates a MuJoCo renderer, so the sim backend needs a display and input devices and was not run here
the observation is the flattened 27-value array of the six kept members; its values are placeholder test data and were not compared with a MuJoCo run
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes get_state but no set_state, and the bridge requires both

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop the runtime refuses step and reset until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the last world state stays readable
